Adversaries may abuse utilities that allow for command execution to bypass security restrictions that limit the use of command-line interpreters.

Adversaries may interact with the Windows Registry to hide configuration information within Registry keys, remove information as part of cleaning up, or as part of other techniques to aid in persistence and execution.
Adversaries may delete or modify artifacts generated within systems to remove evidence of their presence or hinder defenses.
Adversaries may attempt to make an executable or file difficult to discover or analyze by encrypting, encoding, or otherwise obfuscating its contents on the system or in transit.
Adversaries may undermine security controls that will either warn users of untrusted activity or prevent execution of untrusted programs.
Adversaries may attempt to make payloads difficult to discover and analyze by delivering files to victims as uncompiled code.

sigma_analysis_results.rule_title: Dot net compiler compiles file from suspicious location
sigma_analysis_results.rule_description: Dot net compiler compiles file from suspicious location
Detects execution of "csc.exe" to compile .NET code. Attackers often leverage this to compile code on the fly and use it in other stages.

When C# is compiled dynamically, a .cmdline file will be created as a part of the process.
Certain processes are not typically observed compiling C# code, but can do so without touching disk.
This can be used to unpack a payload for execution
